about: What --check asserts for this template beyond the common rules: the planner, the owner, both critics and the integrator ran as their own subagents; the owner was dispatched at least twice (one piece per outer round) and the piece critic at least twice; each critic wrote its own report; the owner and the integrator never read the held-out reference and both critics did; a back edge was taken; PIECES.md ends with every box ticked; the run halts at release-gate. One scripted gate answer, at the decomposition gate only (owner decision 2026-09-22, as for spec-then-loop's first gate in batch one): without it nothing past the planner runs and the design bet cannot be tested. The release gate gets no scripted answer. The design bet (write-up): piece 1's obvious rendering misses properties of the reference that only a side-by-side shows, so e-critic-fail fires at least once, and both pieces end ticked. Amended on 2026-10-04, before the re-proof of the template as slice 0017's reconcile left it (the planner names each piece's reference cut and never copies it), for the two errors the first write-up names in its own expectations: `PIECES.md` is no longer listed as the planner's report alone, because the piece critic ticks its box there by design; and `stop human` is an expected ending beside the halt at release-gate, because the outer loop's human stop comes due after every second piece and the planner may cut more than two. The first run is in run-1/ with the expectations it was checked against.

resume.prompt: Answer at the gate `{{gate}}` of run `{{run-id}}`: {{answer}}. Continue that run from where it halted.
